subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and require a targeted launch-readiness fix, or intentionally serialize/throttle rapid distinct ACPX launches?
rationale: Current code and tests deliberately allow different ACP session keys to run in parallel, so broad serialization would be a product and compatibility choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism
options.body: Require live ACPX/Claude proof and a targeted launch-readiness fix that keeps independent ACP sessions concurrent.

options.title: Throttle ACPX launches
options.body: Serialize or cap rapid distinct ACPX child launches and update tests/docs to make the reduced concurrency contract explicit.

options.title: Wait for fresh proof
options.body: Keep the item blocked on needs-info until a current reproduction identifies whether the old symptom still exists.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism
recommendation.body: Require live ACPX/Claude proof and a targeted launch-readiness fix that keeps independent ACP sessions concurrent.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACPX embedding and current ACP spawn/manager work make this the best available routing owner for the launch-readiness versus concurrency tradeoff.
